definitions.explanation: A soft, flavored substance that is chewed but not swallowed.

examples.japanese: チューインガムを{噛|か}む。
{眠気|ねむけ}{覚|ざ}ましにチューインガムを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought some chewing gum to stay awake.

examples.japanese: チューインガムを{噛|か}みながら{人|ひと}と{話|はな}すのは{失礼|しつれい}だと{言|い}われることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Chewing gum while talking to someone is often considered rude.

notes:
A loanword from English "chewing gum." In everyday conversation, the shortened form ガム is far more common. チューインガム is the formal, full-length term seen on product packaging and in official contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チューインガムを{噛|か}む: to chew gum
- チューインガムを{捨|す}てる: to throw away gum
- チューインガムを{吐|は}き{出|だ}す: to spit out gum
- {板|いた}ガム: stick gum (flat rectangular pieces)
- {粒|つぶ}ガム: pellet gum (coated pieces)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ガム: gum — the everyday abbreviated form, used much more frequently in speech
- {風船|ふうせん}ガム: bubble gum — gum specifically designed for blowing bubbles
